purpose: Research demonstration; no interviews, recruitment or user observations took place.

codebook.name: Unclear state and next action
codebook.include: Confusion between queued, held and confirmed, or uncertainty about the next action
codebook.exclude: A complaint only about not receiving email
codebook.implication: State the current status, required action and consequence of inaction together

codebook.name: Duplicate registration as insurance
codebook.include: Registering for equivalent sessions to preserve options or avoid missing out
codebook.exclude: Registering for independent events with different content
codebook.implication: Collect acceptable sessions and preferences once; explain the one-seat-per-workshop rule

codebook.name: Manual coordination after cancellation
codebook.include: A manual chain of cancellation, contacting the next person, waiting for a reply and updating a sheet
codebook.implication: Automate backfill with an explanatory log; distinguish an offer from its acceptance

codebook.name: Confirmation windows and notification reach
codebook.include: Classes, work or offline periods make a short hold window unsuitable
codebook.exclude: The event start time itself is unsuitable
codebook.implication: Allow organisers to configure holds and display the deadline clearly

codebook.name: Queue fairness and explainability
codebook.include: Questions about arrival order, preference matching or why another person received a seat first
codebook.exclude: Personal preferences unrelated to allocation rules
codebook.implication: Explain both arrival order and acceptable-session constraints; avoid promising an exact wait

codebook.name: Permissions, data and procurement constraints
codebook.include: Institutional systems, exports, retention, organisation permissions or budget restrictions
codebook.exclude: General feature wishes without a concrete restriction
codebook.implication: Provide CSV export and organisation permissions; validate pricing and procurement separately

interviews.persona: Second-year student with a changing timetable, familiar with forms and group chats
interviews.episode: The same CV workshop runs on Tuesday and Thursday. Concerned about a timetable change, the student registers for both and later cannot find how to cancel one.
interviews.workflow: Opens two forms from a group message, submits both, keeps two confirmation emails and contacts the organiser once the class timetable is settled.
interviews.need: Select both acceptable sessions while occupying only one seat; provide cancellation without searching old emails.
interviews.negative_case: If neither selected session remains suitable, the student must withdraw and register again rather than receive an unselected session.
quotes: I register twice to keep my options, not because I want to attend twice.
A place where I can cancel is more useful than another notification.

interviews.persona: First-year student using a waitlist for the first time
interviews.episode: Submits a waitlist form for a full session but interprets the response receipt as successful registration, only asking the organiser the day before the event.
interviews.workflow: Saves a screenshot after submitting and searches email for confirmation; does not clearly distinguish receipt of a request from a confirmed seat.
interviews.need: State plainly whether a seat is available and whether an acceptance action is required to keep it.
interviews.negative_case: A countdown may increase anxiety; first-time users need to know whether they can remain queued after expiry.
quotes: When I received the form response, I thought I was registered.
What does held mean, and how is it different from confirmed?

interviews.persona: Third-year student on an internship who rarely checks personal email during work
interviews.episode: Receives a backfill email during an internship and sees it at lunch, after the seat has moved to the next person.
interviews.workflow: Disables notifications at work and checks email at lunch rather than keeping the registration page open.
interviews.need: Know the confirmation window before joining, so that the student can choose events whose response requirements are practical.
interviews.negative_case: Fifteen minutes is not universally suitable; automation can repeatedly exclude people unable to respond quickly.
quotes: Automatic relay is useful, but I cannot check my mailbox every fifteen minutes.
Tell me the deadline first so I can judge whether this waitlist works for me.

interviews.persona: Postgraduate student available at one fixed time who prefers simple tools
interviews.episode: Can attend only on Friday. The existing form allows that session to be chosen directly and causes no substantial difficulty.
interviews.workflow: Opens a link, selects the only suitable session, submits and checks the confirmation email.
interviews.need: Keep single-session selection simple without forcing multiple choices or ranking.
interviews.negative_case: For simple events without a waitlist, another login and confirmation step may add more work than the existing form.
quotes: I can only come on Friday; I do not need the system to arrange the other two days.
If the form already works, I do not want to learn a new system just to register.

interviews.persona: Fourth-year student attending career workshops who is concerned about fairness
interviews.episode: A group chat shows that a later registrant received a Thursday seat first. The student accepts only Tuesday but mistakenly believes someone has jumped the queue.
interviews.workflow: Checks group messages and spreadsheet timestamps, then privately asks the organiser about queue order.
interviews.need: Explain that a later registrant who accepts another session may receive a seat first.
interviews.negative_case: One queue number alone cannot explain allocation across sessions; the head of the queue is not guaranteed the next seat in any session.
quotes: Did the other person jump the queue, or did I not choose that time?
I am happy to register once, but I want to understand who receives a seat and why.

interviews.persona: Second-year exchange student who relies on email rather than local group chats
interviews.episode: Misses a backfill message sent only to an infrequently checked group and must find a group administrator to cancel.
interviews.workflow: Bookmarks the event link, checks email and contacts the organiser when the current state is unclear.
interviews.need: Email links should return to the current state; cancellation should show a clear ending and remove obsolete confirmation controls.
interviews.negative_case: Does not want to join a chat group; one notification channel cannot suit everyone.
quotes: The email should take me straight back to my current status.
If I still see the old seat after cancelling, I worry the cancellation did not work.

interviews.persona: Events lead of a student technology club whose team shares a spreadsheet
interviews.episode: Three training sessions share a pool of registrants. Two committee members handle cancellations separately and contact the same waitlisted person twice.
interviews.workflow: Creates three forms, merges email addresses, flags duplicates, checks queue order, contacts people individually and updates all three sheets after acceptance.
interviews.need: All committee members need the same current state; the backfill log should identify the release, the new hold and whether it was accepted.
interviews.negative_case: A monthly fee is unattractive in quiet months; export and permission controls are prerequisites for adoption.
quotes: The difficult part is two people editing the sheet at once without knowing who has contacted whom.
Ten dollars may work when we run events every month, but I do not want to keep paying during the break.

interviews.persona: Student coordinator of a career-development programme whose small team can choose free tools
interviews.episode: An evening session is cancelled at short notice. The team must ask every participant about alternative times because the form did not collect preferences.
interviews.workflow: Downloads registrations, filters confirmed participants, emails them about alternatives and manually assembles waitlist and attendance lists.
interviews.need: Collect acceptable times at registration and reallocate after a session cancellation while keeping a clear history.
interviews.negative_case: An automatically issued offer does not establish attendance; confirmed participants must not be reported as actual attendees.
quotes: The form only asked which day they wanted; after cancellation we realised we did not know their alternatives.
Receiving a backfill offer and actually attending are two different things.

interviews.persona: Departmental student assistant subject to supervisor approval and institutional system requirements
interviews.episode: A departmental training programme already uses an institutional registration system, but waitlisting is handled by email and exporting a participant list requires approval.
interviews.workflow: Exports from the institutional system, creates supporting sheets per training session, contacts waitlisted people and updates the institutional records afterwards.
interviews.need: Clarify data retention, permissions, export and institutional approval before procurement can be considered.
interviews.negative_case: A higher acceptable price does not imply purchasing authority; price interest must not be treated as validated demand.
quotes: The features look useful, but I cannot decide to move the participant list to a new system.
The price is not the main issue; approval and who can export the data are.
